items.headline: New Research Finds Enterprise AI Failures Are Shifting Beyond Hallucinations as Companies Move from Chatbots to Agents
items.summary: ChatSee.ai research analyzing over 10,000 enterprise AI failure events found that hallucination-related failures account for less than 10% of observed failures. The largest failure family is resolution and escalation breakdowns at 31.1% of failures, while execution and action-related failures increased 62% relative to Q2 2024 baseline. As enterprises move from simple chatbots to autonomous agents, the failure modes are shifting from accuracy issues to workflow and process integration problems.

items.headline: EU AI Act 2026 Key Compliance Requirements for Enterprises
items.summary: The most critical compliance deadline is August 2, 2026, when requirements for Annex III high-risk AI systems become enforceable covering AI used in employment, education, essential services, credit scoring, and critical infrastructure. High-risk system providers need risk management systems, data governance, technical documentation, automatic record keeping, transparency to users, human oversight, and post-market monitoring. Non-compliance can result in fines up to EUR 35 million or 7% of global annual turnover, whichever is higher.
